q1_issues.issue: "a while" is a stretch of time, but it is encoded as an ordinary entity witness in the Theme slot (plus a class atom for a kind `while`), so the parse asserts that some object was taken rather than that the eventuality lasts an unspecified extent.

q2_gaps: duration objects of the light verb "take" ("take a while", "takes two hours") — the Measure/duration form requires a magnitude and a unit, so an unquantified duration NP has no licensed encoding and falls through to the generic indefinite-NP rule
an antecedentless demonstrative "that" standing for a situation — the no-antecedent pronoun rule names he/she/they/it only, and event anaphora presupposes an antecedent clause
notes: "could" read as epistemic `(Might e)` at confidence 0.9 with no tense beside it matches the status-predicate rules (though "could" is not itself in the might/probably/must list), and the untyped-referent rule is respected by minting sk_thing_1 with its class atom. Agent on the inanimate subject is per-spec for a transitive.
